newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ human rights panel to study women in military.
newsitem.headline: NZ human rights panel to study women in military.

text.p: The New Zealand Human Rights Commission will examine the integration of women into the New Zealand Defence Force, officials said on Monday.
The "gender integration audit" follows allegations in March of sexual harassment in the navy.

It would aim to identify the Defence Force's philosophy, policies and practices towards the integration of women, Chief of Defence Force Lieutenant General Tony Birks and Chief Human Rights Commissioner Pamela Jefferies said in a joint statement.

The audit, endorsed by Defence Minister Paul East, is separate from an internal Defence Force investigation into allegations of sexual harassment in the navy made in March by former rating Larissa Turner, and from the study of Turner's complaints by the commission.
Turner said she had been verbally and physically harassed constantly during a Middle East Gulf deployment.
Birks said women were an integral part of the Defence Force and he was totally committed to their full integration in their areas of employment.
"Discrimination and harassment of any sort is unacceptable and not tolerated in the Defence Force.

"Not only is it illegal but harassment is a personal affront and is inimical to the development of mutual respect, trust and confidence which are the basis of the small group cohesion on which so much of the Defence Force's effectiveness rests."
The audit, which will cover both military and civilian staff, will be completed by April 30, 1998, and will cost NZ$144,000 (US$100,000).
